groups.sentence: Instructors learn effective prompting techniques and teach students to write and refine prompts, including through assignments.
Prompts with more specificity, context and clear roles give better AI output.
Students refine and revise their prompts through repeated trial and error and do not expect the best result on the first try.
Effective use of AI requires thoughtful, well-crafted prompting, and prompt quality determines output quality.
Students write clear, specific and detailed prompts that give context, and avoid vague, minimal prompts.
Everyone structures prompts with elements such as a role or persona, task, context and format.
Students break complex tasks into parts, set context in the first prompt, and ask follow-up questions or multiple versions.
Users may ask the AI to explain its reasoning, critique its own output or suggest changes with explanations.
Students experiment with different AI tools and familiar subjects to learn their strengths and weaknesses.
Everyone takes care that bias in prompts can skew AI output, and uses specificity to get more diverse outputs.
Everyone provides examples of the desired output or of their own writing so the AI can adapt.
With instructor approval, students may use AI platforms to learn prompt engineering.
Everyone learns about prompt engineering and how to write prompts that work.
